land.text: the city of Mari and its surroundings, the seat of the Akkadian-appointed Shakkanakku (a 60 km disc around Tell Hariri)

predecessors.note: Mari was destroyed by Sargon (the mari dossier ends -2290; the akkadian-empire dossier gains the middle Euphrates then) and was 'deserted for two generations' before Manishtushu restored it under a Shakkanakku, Ididish (the Mari page's first Shakkanakku, c. 2266). Akkad kept direct control until Shar-kali-sharri's reign.

land.text: the Euphrates around Mari that the Lim dynasty takes as its seat c. 1830 BC (the Lim dossier's first shape)

successors.note: The Mari page: c. 1830 BC Mari becomes the seat of the Amorite Lim dynasty under Yaggid-Lim; strong continuity between the Shakkanakku and Amorite eras (paraphrased). The lim-dynasty-of-mari dossier starts at -1830 with counterpart 'nobody', so it records no gain from the Shakkanakku.

capitals.name: Mari (Tell Hariri)
capitals.note: Infobox coordinates 34 32 58 N, 40 53 24 E near Abu Kamal, Deir ez-Zor; the Shakkanakku palace of the third city. Same point as in the mari and lim-dynasty-of-mari dossiers.

correction.text: the city of Mari and its surroundings, the seat of the Akkadian-appointed Shakkanakku (a 60 km disc around Tell Hariri)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Shakkanakku row. The page says Mari was restored by Manishtushu, that Akkad kept direct control and installed a Shakkanakku, and dates the first one, Ididish, c. 2266 BC (a 60-year reign on the lists, after which the post became hereditary); it describes no territory (and the Shakkanakku page is a stub), so only the city's own surroundings are drawn: 40 cells, about 10,100 km2 by the gazetteer, the same disc the mari dossier uses for the first city. The infobox area (60 ha) is the tell, not a state.

correction.text: Mari and the middle Euphrates, as the mari dossier's successor note reads them: the Euphrates within 40 km through Dayr Az Zawr and Al-Anbar; the page itself describes no territory

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Independent under Shar-kali-sharri (the Mari page, paraphrased: when Akkad disintegrated under Shar-kali-sharri, Mari became independent but kept the Shakkanakku title), nominally under Ur's hegemony in the Ur III period, to c. 1830. The extent is the mari dossier's successor-note reading (180 cells, about 45,500 km2); the page gives none, the Ur III page says only of its northern and western periphery that it had 'fluctuating boundaries' and that in the Khabur valley the kingdoms of Urkesh and Nagar remained autonomous. One shape for 390 years because no page dates a change of extent.

region.text: the city of Mari and its surroundings, the seat of the Akkadian-appointed Shakkanakku (a 60 km disc around Tell Hariri)

ledger.note: 2266 BCE: Ididish, the first Shakkanakku on the lists, governs a restored Mari for Akkad. The page dates him c. 2266 BC, says Mari 'was deserted for two generations' after Sargon, then restored by Manishtushu, with a military governor installed by Akkad (the page says Akkad kept direct control). The year is the page's; the 60 km disc is the researcher's reading, since the page gives no land.

region.text: the middle Euphrates outside the Mari disc, which Mari holds once it is independent under Shar-kali-sharri

ledger.note: 2217 BCE: Mari becomes independent as Akkad disintegrates. The Mari page says, paraphrased, that Mari became independent but kept the Shakkanakku title when Akkad disintegrated under Shar-kali-sharri; the Akkadian Empire page gives his reign as 2218-2193 BC ('came to power around 2217 BC'). No year is given for the independence itself, so the accession year is bridged; the land (the middle Euphrates) is the mari dossier's reading. The akkadian-empire dossier gains this land at -2290 and records no loss.

region.text: the downstream and outlying Euphrates of the Shakkanakku shape that the Lim shape does not reach

ledger.note: 1830 BCE: the Shakkanakku state ends and the Euphrates outside the Lim seat is left unattributed. The page says the dynasty ended for unknown reasons shortly before the Lim dynasty, in the second half of the 19th century BC, and gives no territory for either, so the land beyond the Lim dossier's first shape is recorded as nobody's (page silent).

region.text: the Euphrates around Mari that the Lim dynasty takes as its seat c. 1830 BC (the Lim dossier's first shape)

ledger.note: 1830 BCE: the Shakkanakku dynasty gives way to the Amorite Lim dynasty at Mari. the page says that around 1830 BC Mari became the seat of the Amorite Lim dynasty under Yaggid-Lim; by c. 1820 BC Yahdun-Lim was firmly in control; the page finds strong continuity (paraphrased) between the Shakkanakku and Amorite eras and names no last Shakkanakku.

certainty.note: The page gives no territory for the Shakkanakku state; the middle Euphrates is the researcher's reading, and the Ur III periphery had 'fluctuating boundaries'.

sources.title: Mari, Syria
sources.note: Shakkanakku period (city III): Manishtushu's restoration, Ididish c. 2266 BC, hereditary post, independence under Shar-kali-sharri, nominal Ur hegemony, end of the dynasty before the Lim dynasty c. 1830 BC; infobox coordinates and area (60 ha). The page gives no territory for the Shakkanakku state.

sources.title: Shakkanakku
sources.note: A stub on the title: no start or end dates for the dynasty, no first or last ruler, no Ur III; only Ishtup-Ilum c. 2150, Iddi-Ilum c. 2090, Tura-Dagan c. 2071-2051, Puzur-Ishtar c. 2050 BC and that Shakkanakkus were considered 'Kings' from Apil-Kin.

sources.title: Akkadian Empire
sources.note: Shar-kali-sharri's reign 2218-2193 BC (came to power around 2217 BC); control of peripheral regions 'sporadic and uneven'; no Shakkanakku, Ididish or Manishtushu's restoration in the text.

sources.title: Third Dynasty of Ur
sources.note: Mari as Ur III's western partner: 'Mari was once conquered by the kings of Akkad, but the kings of Ur preferred a peaceful relation'; Shulgi married a princess of Mari; periphery of military governors with 'fluctuating boundaries'; no dates for the relation.

notes:
Shakkanakku Kingdom of Mari (c. 2266-1830 BC, middle Euphrates), the 'Second Kingdom' or third city of Mari between the mari dossier (ends -2290) and the lim-dynasty-of-mari dossier (starts -1830); Cliopatria has no row. Four pages opened; the Shakkanakku page is a stub.

To settle: (1) No page gives a territory for the Shakkanakku state; the extent is the mari dossier's reading of Mari and the middle Euphrates (Euphrates within 40 km through Dayr Az Zawr and Al-Anbar), and the early shape is only the 60 km disc around Tell Hariri. (2) Independence: the Mari page puts it under Shar-kali-sharri without a year; -2217 is the accession year of the Akkadian Empire page (reign 2218-2193), confidence 1. The akkadian-empire dossier gains the middle Euphrates at -2290 (Sargon destroys Mari) and has no loss at independence; its -2250/-2200 keyframes are Cliopatria shapes and may still contain the Euphrates, so the Akkad outline overlaps this one from -2266. (3) Ur III: the Mari page calls Mari nominally under Ur's hegemony; the Ur III page says Shulgi married a princess of Mari and the kings of Ur preferred peaceful relations; no date or territorial event, and the third-dynasty-of-ur dossier has no vassal_start for this state (a suzerain-side event it may want, counterpart 'shakkanakku-kingdom-of-mari'). Not recorded here, because a vassal event belongs to the suzerain. (4) End: no last Shakkanakku, no cause, 'second half of the 19th century BC' for the dynasty's end; -1830 is the Lim seat date. The lim-dynasty-of-mari dossier takes 'nobody' as counterpart at -1830. (5) Rulers are not listed: the Mari page names only Ididish (c. 2266, a 60-year reign) and the Shakkanakku page gives a few dated rulers (Ishtup-Ilum c. 2150, Iddi-Ilum c. 2090, Tura-Dagan c. 2071-2051, Puzur-Ishtar c. 2050) without a full list. (6) Gazetteer names used (Mari, Euphrates, Dayr Az Zawr, Al-Anbar) all resolve.
